benchmarks.name: AA-Briefcase
benchmarks.response_type: Agentic task completion with file outputs
benchmarks.scoring: Combined Elo from pairwise comparisons on rubric-graded task success, analytical quality, and presentation quality
benchmarks.harness: Stirrup in E2B sandbox (offline, code_exec, finish, abandon_task_finish)
benchmarks.grader: Panel of 3 judges (Claude Opus 4.8 max effort, GPT-5.5 high, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview high)
benchmarks.source_license: Proprietary benchmark with public Lite sample

contamination_protection.design: Internal scenario pools mixing real, augmented, and synthetic workplace files
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Underlying business documents derive from public filings, transcripts, and open data; teacher models in judge panel share training distributions with frontier evaluated models

benchmarks.name: GDPval-AA v2
benchmarks.response_type: Agentic task completion with file outputs
benchmarks.scoring: Pairwise Bradley-Terry Elo anchored to human experts at 1000; normalized as clamp((Elo - 500) / 2000)
benchmarks.harness: Stirrup in E2B sandbox (6 tools: Web Fetch, Web Search via Brave, View Image, Code Exec, Finish, Abandon Task)
benchmarks.source_license: OpenAI GDPval Gold (MIT / CC-BY where published); AA implementation proprietary
benchmarks.source_provenance: OpenAI GDPval dataset (arXiv:2510.04374) evaluated under AA Stirrup harness

contamination_protection.design: 220 gold tasks public, expanded environment and strict sandboxing
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Public 220 tasks widely available in public GitHub / Hugging Face repos since late 2025; models may memorize reference files and Office document structures

benchmarks.name: τ³-Banking
benchmarks.response_type: Dual control agent-user simulation with knowledge retrieval
benchmarks.grader: GPT-5.4 Mini (medium reasoning) for user simulator and NL assertion judge

contamination_protection.design: Evaluates DB state mutations rather than text utterances
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Public repo code and task policies can be indexed; simulator LLM behavior may shift across API revisions

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench v2.1
benchmarks.harness: Terminus 2 agent harness in E2B sandbox

contamination_protection.design: Containerized tasks with private execution sidecars
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Curated tasks are open source; code and solutions exist in public git commits and scraping corpora

benchmarks.name: SciCode (v1.0.1)
benchmarks.response_type: Python Code (must pass all unit tests)
benchmarks.scoring: pass@1 sub-problem scoring with scientist-annotated background prompting

contamination_protection.design: Complex multi-step problems with scientist background; regraded in v1.0.1
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Public GitHub test set; known test bugs addressed in SciCode-Verified (arXiv:2608.01655)

benchmarks.name: AA-Omniscience
benchmarks.scoring: AA-Omniscience Index (points for correct, penalty for hallucinated, neutral for abstention)
benchmarks.grader: GPT-5.6 Luna (medium reasoning) for 4-way classification (CORRECT, INCORRECT, PARTIAL_ANSWER, NOT_ATTEMPTED)

contamination_protection.design: 6,000 questions across 42 topics with private held-out test keys
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Factual knowledge questions inevitably overlap with Wikipedia, Wikidata, and common crawl web pre-training data

benchmarks.name: GDP.pdf
benchmarks.response_type: Free-form answer grounded in a long PDF
benchmarks.scoring: All-pass headline (all 500 attempts pass all criteria); Mean Pass secondary
benchmarks.harness: Single turn, text via LiteParse+OCR and 72-150 DPI page composite images
benchmarks.grader: GPT-5.6 Luna (medium reasoning) independent criterion evaluations

contamination_protection.design: Long complex real-world PDFs across 10 domains
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Source PDFs (SEC filings, municipal reports, public agency PDFs) are freely available on public web and frequently crawled during model pretraining

benchmarks.name: AA-LCR v1.1
benchmarks.harness: ~100k input tokens per question across ~230 documents

contamination_protection.design: Synthesized and curated multi-document contexts; v1.1 corrected 16 answer keys
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Public reports and consultations used as context documents exist in public web scrapes
Subject to known adversarial curation bias (filtered against GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, o1); questions may leak into open community datasets

benchmarks.name: CritPt
benchmarks.response_type: Python Functions, Symbolic Expressions, Numerical Answers
benchmarks.scoring: pass@1 across 5 repeats of 70 challenge questions
benchmarks.harness: Two-step parsing (reasoning step + answer formatting step)

contamination_protection.design: Unpublished problems created by 50+ physicists; private official grading server
contamination_protection.leakage_risks: Prompts are public; answers are private on grading server, but repeated API queries could allow answer extraction or distillation if query auditing is lax

standalone_evaluations.name: Harvey LAB-AA
standalone_evaluations.split: private (120 private tasks held by Harvey; 5 public examples)
standalone_evaluations.harness: Stirrup in Linux sandbox (read-only documents, no internet)
standalone_evaluations.grader: Gemini 3.1 Pro (single judge, atomic binary rubric)
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: High task privacy, but legal statutes and standard deal structures exist in legal corpora

standalone_evaluations.name: APEX-Agents-AA
standalone_evaluations.split: public subset (452 of 480 tasks from mercor/apex-agents)
standalone_evaluations.harness: Stirrup in Archipelago environment with MCP tools
standalone_evaluations.grader: Archipelago local file grader + Gemini 3 Flash (low reasoning) judge
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: Tasks are derived from public release; risk of web/git memorization is moderate to high

standalone_evaluations.name: AutomationBench-AA
standalone_evaluations.split: private held-out split from Zapier AutomationBench v1.0
standalone_evaluations.harness: AutomationBench multi-turn environment with REST APIs
standalone_evaluations.grader: Programmatic assertions on environment state (objectives and guardrails)
metrics: Objective completion percentage (zero credit on guardrail failure)
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: Private split prevents verbatim prompt memorization, but standard SaaS API schemas (Slack, Gmail, Jira) are in pre-training data

standalone_evaluations.name: AA-AnalystAgent
standalone_evaluations.grader: Gemini 3 Flash (reasoning) + deterministic numeric equivalence override
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: Privately held files and questions provide strong barrier against public crawl, but standard financial/statistical formulas are universal

standalone_evaluations.name: ITBench-AA
standalone_evaluations.split: hybrid (40 public IBM SRE tasks + 19 private tasks)
standalone_evaluations.harness: Stirrup sandbox with offline Kubernetes snapshot
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: 40 tasks are public; 19 private tasks offer limited protection from K8s architecture generalization

standalone_evaluations.name: EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA
standalone_evaluations.harness: Stirrup sandbox with MCP gym servers and SQLite DBs
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: Synthetic database seeds reduce memorization, but schema patterns are public in ServiceNow release

standalone_evaluations.name: IFBench
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: Publicly released test set; high risk of inclusion in alignment and instruction-tuning datasets

standalone_evaluations.name: MLCR-AA
standalone_evaluations.split: private held-out set (expert + compound tiers from Wisedocs)
standalone_evaluations.grader: Conciseness gate (<5x ref len) + 3-judge majority vote
standalone_evaluations.contamination_assessment: Private split shields exact clinical questions, but synthetic clinical cases mirror standard medical textbooks

registry_status.notes: Already present in data/manual/benchmarks-aa.yaml with 113 observed models
ActualAnalysis tracks 64 whole-problem pass@1 under SciCode-Verified v2, whereas AA v4.2 evaluates 288 subproblem pass@1 under SciCode v1.0.1
Both use 97 items; AA uses 5 repeats and GPT-5.4 Mini judge, whereas actualanalysis specifies default_k: 4
Both use 89 items; AA uses Terminus 2 with 3 repeats, whereas actualanalysis holds it as vendor-reported watchlist
ActualAnalysis uses CAIS 2500-item split, whereas AA v4.2 evaluates 2158 text-only subset with GPT-5.6 Luna equality checker
data/benchmarks/aa-lcr.yaml explicitly states: Artificial Analysis scores themselves are prohibited; this entry permits only non-AA runs
data/benchmarks/gdpval.yaml explicitly commands: Never ingest GDPval-AA
Grok owns registry additions; AA-Briefcase is an Elo metric (~1000-1400) which fails DisplayBenchmarkFileSchema 0-100 range
Grok owns registry additions; composite metric (Accuracy + Non-hallucination) needs schema adapter
Registry only contains Google model card specific entry; AA GDP.pdf uses 500 attempts across 1275 criteria evaluated by GPT-5.6 Luna

admission_blocker_analysis.conclusion: Cannot admit new AA benchmark suite into data/manual/benchmarks-aa.yaml without breaking schema and violating repository policy

technical_blockers.issue: Schema strictly defines a single benchmark metadata block. There is no list or dictionary structure to hold 10 benchmarks.
Schema enforces percent scale bounded in [0, 100]. AA-Briefcase and GDPval-AA v2 are Elo scores (~1000-1400+), which fail validation.
Rows whose benchmark_id is not in data/benchmarks/*.yaml are silently dropped. grok owns registry audit so we cannot add missing benchmarks.
README explicitly designates CritPt as the benchmark display overlay and isolates it strictly from CC-BY snapshots and capability fits.
Explicit prohibitions: data/benchmarks/aa-lcr.yaml forbids AA scores; data/benchmarks/gdpval.yaml forbids GDPval-AA.

admission_blocker_analysis.resolution_taken: Staged full candidate in ignored work/coverage-expansion/aa/benchmarks-candidate.yaml and documented blockers.

independent_alternatives.author_results_summary: Base models reach ~4.0% (GPT-5 high); tool-augmented runs reach ~10%; human PhD experts reach ~65% vs skilled non-experts ~34%.
Original SciCode main problem resolve rate: Claude 3.5 Sonnet ~4.6%, o1-preview ~7.7%. SciCode-Verified v2 provides corrected 64 whole-problem evaluations.
Published by Sierra Research; measures pass@1 against transactional backend database states with ~700 policy documents.
Maintained by Stanford and Laude Institute across 89 curated terminal tasks; pass@1 graded by verification suites.
Published by OpenAI across 44 occupations; 220 gold tasks open-sourced, 1,320 tasks full suite; scored via human expert pairwise evaluation.
Published by Surge AI; 100 professional tasks over 4,592 PDF pages; original Surge AI harness uses raw PDF with Gemini 3.5 Flash judge.
Center for AI Safety (CAIS) and Scale AI; 2,500-question multidisciplinary exam designed to resist LLM shortcut solutions.

implementable_next_steps.action: Audit and expand data/benchmarks/ to introduce official benchmark definitions for aa-briefcase, aa-omniscience, and general gdp-pdf, while clarifying policies on aa-lcr and gdpval.
Evolve DisplayBenchmarkFileSchema in apps/web/lib/display-data.ts to support a multi-benchmark manifest (e.g. benchmarks array or dictionary) and support both percent and Elo score scales.
Migrate staged candidates from work/coverage-expansion/aa/benchmarks-candidate.yaml into data/manual/benchmarks-aa.yaml once the schema and registry blockers are resolved.

Ingest independently published non-AA author results for SciCode-Verified, CAIS HLE, Stanford Terminal-Bench, and Sierra tau3-bench to enrich the public CC-BY capability fit without proprietary AA licensing entanglements.
